basis: local code, local dataset, own GPU experiments; no network used after user requested offline work

input_checkpoint.note: generated by current code with default 30k schedule; training time is input preparation, not a controlled comparison; checkpoint deleted after analysis

depth_compaction.method: Count Gaussian pairs/depth keys at full capacity; compact 128-slot clusters containing at least one positive pair count in ascending pool order; choose quarter/half/full sort capacity; gather positive keys and IDs, pad with uint32 max / ID -1, stable depth-sort; padded IDs have zero count; retain original count/emit/stable tile-sort/range pipeline and public output shapes. Last partial 64-slot cluster is padded for cluster reduction and guarded when gathering.
depth_compaction.protocol: capacity 1M, SH3, 8x16 tiles, 8M pair arena, four views 0/48/96/144; retain every tenth complete cluster as distributed sparse control plus full model; 30 warmup and six alternating rounds of 200 calls for baseline, dynamic candidate and static-bucket diagnostic; includes host dispatch
depth_compaction.correctness: For all eight cases, pair count, overflow, valid Gaussian ID prefix, tile offsets and point counts equal baseline exactly. Static diagnostic additionally checks ID prefix and offsets. Padding tails are undefined and not compared.
depth_compaction.static_diagnostic_limit: Bucket chosen using a CPU oracle before compilation; not a viable adaptive training implementation. It is only an overhead diagnostic.
depth_compaction.gpu_monitoring_limit: GPU exclusive permission and process checks before/after; unlike the later probes, this exploratory sort run did not continuously monitor other compute processes.
depth_compaction.status: rejected; dynamic version slower in all eight cases; no production edits

heavy_tile_ablation.protocol: same projected arrays, image gradient, supplied scale, transmittance and last contributors; keep only selected tiles and remap absolute pair indices; no-statistics backward; 30 warmup calls, 6 alternating rounds of 150 calls; includes output clearing and host dispatch
heavy_tile_ablation.interpretation: Workload ablation, not a valid faster rendering algorithm. The selected tiles retain original Gaussian order, pixel gradients, final transmittance and last contributors; absolute pair indices are remapped. Timings retain output clearing and all-tile input reads, so the 69% elapsed ratio cannot be attributed entirely to the single tile. It supports a serial heavy-tile tail.

fixed_count.protocol: same fresh million-capacity NPZ, view 0, SH3, Optax, fixed density, 8M pairs, 30 warmup and 500 timed steps; three alternating rounds; no other GPU compute process before or during runs; monitor every 0.5 seconds

full_training.protocol: production default 30k schedule, images_4, 169 training / 25 held-out views, seed 0, 1M capacity, 8M pairs, only tile shape differs; three alternating rounds; native and common 8x16 renderer evaluation; no other GPU compute process before or during any run; monitor every 0.5 seconds
full_training.quality_limits: Three runs per tile shape on one scene and one seed. Mean PSNR is slightly lower for 8x8, inside the observed 8x16 run range; these samples do not establish quality equivalence across scenes.

tile_shape.status: verified optional benchmark configuration; default 8x16 retained because only one scene was tested, pair pressure increases and a small measured quality difference remains

pixel_group_backward.protocol: same 8x16 visibility table and forward cache; one warp per pixel-pair group; replay original vertical power differences to preserve per-pixel alpha; no-statistics backward, symmetric conic, 30 warmup, six alternating rounds of 150 calls; includes output clearing and host dispatch

whole_step.protocol: same fresh million-capacity NPZ, view 0, SH3, Optax, fixed density, 8x16 tiles, 8M pairs, only backward pixel-group scheduling differs; 30 warmup and 500 timed steps; three alternating rounds; no other GPU compute process before or during runs; monitor every 0.5 seconds

regression.command: temporary launch_backward substitution, then pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_packed.py tests/test_work_balance.py tests/test_nnx.py tests/test_call_interfaces.py tests/test_production_training.py
regression.reason: Statistics mode retained the old warp reduction while the ordinary VJP split pixel groups; changing the half2 reduction order violated the existing internal gradient consistency tolerance. Tests were not weakened.

pixel_group_backward.status: rejected; no production source changes and no full-training speed or quality claim for this prototype

next_algorithm_priority.proposal: Split heavy backward jobs while sharing the same per-pixel alpha/transmittance sequence and keeping one gradient reduction convention across statistics and ordinary VJP paths. Only heavy jobs need finer partitioning; avoid growing the pair arena for all tiles.
next_algorithm_priority.limits: The tested independent-warp split did not preserve the current half2 reduction convention. A cooperative reduction or checkpointed segment design needs its own correctness and full-training validation before merge.

segment_composition_real_arithmetic.order: A is in front of B; maintain depth order
segment_composition_real_arithmetic.floating_point_limit: Associative in real arithmetic, not bit-exact under current half2 rounding and early termination. Reordering changes must be measured, not assumed safe.
